$comment: Single source of truth for the prebuilt dependency toolchain.
Application builds NEVER compile Qt or any other dependency. They consume
the artifacts pinned here, which are produced by
.github/workflows/toolchain-build.yml and published to a GitHub Release
(archives) or GHCR (container images).
To upgrade dependencies: change vcpkg.json, run the toolchain workflow,
and merge the pin update it produces. That is the only
moment Qt gets compiled.
'asset' names carry the run that produced them, so publishing a new
toolchain never overwrites the one pinned here. The workflow retires the
superseded archives only after this file has been updated on main.
There is no toolchain version. Everything that affects dependency ABI is
part of the cache fingerprint, so a rebuild is triggered by content rather
than by a number someone has to remember to bump.
Container 'image' is the bare package name, NOT a full registry path.
The owner is supplied at runtime from github.repository_owner so this
file is identical in ehb54/ultrascan3 and in any fork: each publishes to
its own GHCR namespace and pins the digest its own toolchain run produced.
The vcpkg commit is NOT recorded here. It is builtin-baseline in
vcpkg.json -- one SHA in the repository, so the ports baseline and the
checked-out vcpkg tool can never drift apart. Checking out that commit
also pins the tool, because bootstrap-vcpkg resolves the tool version
from scripts/vcpkg-tool-metadata.txt at whatever is checked out.
THE PINS BELOW ARE INTENTIONALLY EMPTY.
A toolchain is published to the repository that builds it -- release
assets and GHCR images both live under that owner. Carrying another
repository's pins here would point application builds at artifacts they
cannot fetch, so the fields are blank until this repository runs the
toolchain workflow for the first time.
Merging that first run is what populates them: this file, vcpkg.json, the
triplets and buildsys/docker are all in the workflow's push-paths filter,
so the merge triggers a toolchain build, which validates its own pin
against every target and merges the update automatically.
Until then application builds fail with a clear message from
scripts/fetch-toolchain.sh rather than a download error.
